key_insight: SurgRec presents a scalable, reproducible pretraining recipe for surgical video understanding, demonstrated via two variants (SurgRec-MAE and SurgRec-JEPA) trained on a large multi-source corpus of 10,535 videos (~214.5M frames). It shows that scaling dataset size and a standardized pipeline substantially improves foundation-model readiness for surgical tasks.
problem_solved: Existing surgical foundation models are limited by small, heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent evaluation, and lack of reproducible training pipelines, hindering broad transfer and reliable benchmarking.
method: Curate a large, multi-source surgical video corpus (10,535 videos, ~214.5M frames) to increase scale and procedural diversity.
Design a reproducible pretraining recipe instantiated as SurgRec-MAE (masked autoencoder style) and SurgRec-JEPA (joint-embedding predictive architecture).
Provide an end-to-end, shareable training pipeline and evaluation protocol to enable consistent benchmarking and downstream transfer.
impact: Enables ML practitioners and clinical researchers to build more robust, generalizable surgical foundation models by leveraging large-scale, standardized pretraining and reproducible workflows—accelerating downstream tasks like action recognition, phase detection, and tool localization.
